stem:
Asha holds a bar magnet near a steel paper clip on the table. The clip jumps to the magnet without the magnet touching it first.

Which claim correctly classifies the force between the magnet and the clip?

options.text: It is a non-contact force because the magnet acts on the clip without physical contact.
It is a contact force because forces that act without touching are called contact forces.
It is a contact force because the magnet and the clip will touch after the clip jumps.
It is a non-contact force only while the clip is already moving toward the magnet.

teacher.key_rationale: Magnetic force between magnet and clip acts without contact, so it is non-contact. Calling without-touch forces contact reverses the classification. Treating later touching as required contact drops the without-contact condition. Limiting non-contact to while the clip is already moving over-narrows the rule.

mx_swap.reason: Gravity/Earth CWO invents nouns not in the stem; used relationship_reversal on the contact/non-contact labels instead.
